title: content_grouping.dart groupItemsByNextLevel's maxBrowseDepth clamp silently reintroduces fixed bug R5-6
rule: Evans (invariant re-derived, not enforced once) / doc-reality drift

evidence.quote: if (maxBrowseDepth != null && currentDepth >= maxBrowseDepth) return const [];

/// Pass [maxBrowseDepth] to stop at a particular depth (Browse Content caps at
/// `CurriculumLabels.maxBrowseDepth`).

// The old `>= maxBrowseDepth → return []` conflated "don't drill further"
// with "show nothing"; this fixes R5-6.

why: docs/_archive/superseded/bug-hunt-round5-findings-2026-05-31.md rates R5-6 'high': the browse tree showed 'No content' instead of the terminal chapter rows when a deep-link opened at max browse depth. That bug was fixed only in content_hierarchy_screen.dart's private, hand-duplicated `_groupItemsByNextLevel` (clamp to maxBrowseDepth-1, never return empty) — the fix was never ported back to the 'canonical' shared groupItemsByNextLevel this file exports, which still has the pre-fix `return const []` guard. Repo-wide grep confirms zero current callers pass maxBrowseDepth (Browse Content uses its own private copy instead, precisely because of this bug), so it's a dead branch today — but the doc comment explicitly invites a future caller to wire it up for exactly the Browse Content use case, which would resurrect the regression with zero warning.
recommendation: Either delete content_hierarchy_screen.dart's private duplicate and make it call this shared function (after porting the maxBrowseDepth-1 clamp fix here), or fix the clamp here to match and correct the doc comment so it doesn't claim Browse Content already caps through this parameter.
acceptance_criteria: A test at test/core/content/content_grouping_test.dart calls groupItemsByNextLevel with currentDepth == maxBrowseDepth and asserts it returns the clamped terminal-level rows, not an empty list (regression for R5-6).
content_hierarchy_screen.dart no longer maintains a second, independently-fixed copy of this grouping logic.
